pr_title: Made Editor Log buttons save their state, per project.
pr_body:
Closes #48445

State is saved in `res://.godot/editor_layout.cfg`, which is the same as the editor docks layout, per project. This seems to be the most appropriate place to save it. A slight logic change was required in `EditorNode` so that the file is not overwritten every time it is saved, since now the file is read and written to from somewhere other than the one `EditorNode` method.

The state of all 4 filter buttons and the collapse state is saved:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/41730826/117087152-ff4c8480-ad91-11eb-9636-45ee11673f6b.png)

A timer is used to delay the save, as is done in other places in the editor, so that rapid changes to the state do not spam saving the config file.

CC @KoBeWi
pr_comments:
- Collapse messages seems to be not stored properly.
- Saving the search bar visibility would be useful too.
- Seems like all messages are disabled by default. Should be the opposite, to avoid confusion.

@KoBeWi 
> * Collapse messages seems to be not stored properly.

~I cannot reproduce. Toggling collapse saves the file as expected. If I open the file in VS Code, it automatically updates when it gets changed. I can see the value updating as I change the `collapse` option, as expected. The state of this option appears to be correctly restored when opening the editor again.~ ~Hol up, I may have found the issue.~ Yep, sorry, collapse was being restored properly - I just wasn't updating the button state.

> * Saving the search bar visibility would be useful too.

Added.

> * Seems like all messages are disabled by default. Should be the opposite, to avoid confusion.

I cannot reproduce. Delete `res://.godot/editor_layout.cfg` -> restart editor -> all filters are enabled.

From my testing, the log filter buttons are disabled by default on newly created projects. Would it be possible to enable them by default instead, to get behavior similar to `3.x`? Right now, it's possible to miss important error/warning messages, and your `print()`s won't appear by default when you run the project.

Oops, I thought I fixed that.

Actually, looking above it looks like I couldn't reproduce? Not sure what happened, but I could reproduce just now. 🤷‍♂️
